thread:
incident-bot: Paging on-call for P99 streaming latency breach for customer Ravenback (single-tenant). Affected route: /v1/stream?model=redwood-llama-13b. Observed p99 > 2s over last 12m. SLO p99 = 1s. Incident INC-2026-4059. @maria you are on-call. :rotating_light:

maria (oncall): ack I'm on it. pulling up dashboards and traces now. can someone confirm concurrent sessions for Ravenback? first step: can we route them to fallback or throttle?

lee (infra): seeing dedicated-pool-3 under high load. concurrency for Ravenback = ~350 live sessions (baseline ~60). KV cache eviction spiking, per-node eviction rate: 
```
node-7 evict_rate=520/s
node-8 evict_rate=490/s
node-6 evict_rate=610/s
```
looks like long prefixes / repeating keys are thrashing the prefix KV cache.

maria (oncall): thanks. quick metrics from the console: p50 80ms, p95 420ms, p99 2.1s. streaming stalls consistently around token ~512. impact window started 2026-03-15T12:34Z. customer is single-tenant so high concurrency hits same dedicated pool. propose: 1) enable prefix-KV pin for Ravenback, 2) throttle concurrency to 150 for their API key, 3) route a portion to quantized fallback variant. anyone object?

sam (eng-sre): agree with plan. i'll apply the route patch and set throttles. executing quick patch now: 
```
curl -X POST "https://api.redwood-infra.internal/routes/ravenback" -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPS_TOKEN" -d '{
  "concurrency_limit": 150,
  "kv_pin": true,
  "fallback_model": "redwood-llama-13b-quant",
  "note": "temp mitigation INC-2026-4059"
}'
```

incident-bot: Route patch applied by sam at 2026-03-15T12:46Z. Telemetry shows immediate partial improvement: p99 dropped to ~1.1s within 2m. :thumbsup:

lee (infra): rolling restart of 3 nodes in dedicated-pool-3 started to reclaim fragmented KV memory (drain -> restart -> join). draining node-6 first. draining logs: 
```
2026-03-15T12:48:03 node-6 drain start
2026-03-15T12:48:12 migrating 42 sessions
2026-03-15T12:49:05 node-6 restart complete
```

maria (oncall): good. early customer impact assessment: ~8% of Ravenback requests during the window experienced visible latency degradation (above 1s). No 5xx error spike observed, mainly tail stalls. CS notified. taylor can you confirm customer outreach?

taylor (se): confirmed, CS contacted Ravenback at 12:55Z with temporary mitigations and ETA. Ravenback reports degraded UX in long-chat scenarios, mainly when users hit 40+ message turns (long cumulative prefix). They asked for ETA to full mitigation and rollback plan.

sam (eng-sre): digging into traces — the heavy tail correlates to repeated long system messages that replicate near-identical KV keys (same prefix tokens repeated across sessions). trace sample: 
```
trace_id=abc123 span=kv.lookup key="sys:LONG_CONTEXT:sha256:..." duration=340ms
trace_id=def456 span=kv.lookup key="sys:LONG_CONTEXT:sha256:..." duration=420ms
```
This explains thrash: different sessions repeatedly miss and re-pop the same large prefix entries.

maria (oncall): mitigation status: prefix-KV pin applied, concurrency throttle active, fallback routing enabled, rolling restarts in progress. Observed p99 ~1.0-1.2s post-mitigation. ETA to stabilization ~20-30m. Next steps: 1) keep pin and throttle for 1h, 2) follow-up with a dedicated runbook to handle long-prefix single-tenant customers, 3) recommend model quantization and batching adjustments to Ravenback.

lee (infra): also bumping pool capacity by +2 nodes to absorb burst; autoscaler policy review scheduled.

rachel (support): status page update posted. Customer facing note: "We're seeing elevated latency for long-chat sessions; mitigations in place and engineers are actively investigating." Ravenback CS rep will get hourly updates.

maria (oncall): raising incident severity to Sev2 given customer degradation and business impact. creating ticket INC-2026-4059 in tracker and tagging eng-runtime and devex for follow-up. Handing off active monitoring to sam (eng-sre) for next shift. Handoff summary: 
- What happened: p99 streaming tail spike due to KV cache thrash from long repeated prefixes + 6x normal concurrency.
- Impact: ~8% requests degraded, window 12:34-13:10Z, no errors, streaming stalls at ~512 tokens.
- Actions taken: prefix-KV pin enabled, concurrency limit set to 150, fallback model routing enabled, rolling restart of 3 nodes, +2 nodes added to pool, customer notified.
- Open actions: create runbook for single-tenant long-prefix mitigation, autoscaler policy tweak, post-incident follow-up with Ravenback on batching/quantization.

sam (eng-sre): ack taking over. i'll monitor p99 for 2h and coordinate the postmortem. will also add sampling hooks to capture offending prompt samples (scrubbed) for analysis. :wave:

taylor (se): thanks team. please follow up with CS once postmortem timeline is set.

maria (oncall): handing off complete. logging final note to thread and incident ticket. :white_check_mark:

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026-4059 updated: severity=Sev2, owner=sam, status=monitoring.

sam (eng-sre): I'll create the follow-up runbook PR and schedule a cross-team postmortem for tomorrow. monitoring live metrics now.

rachel (support): adding case note to Ravenback ticket and flagging for account manager.

sam (eng-sre): monitoring shows p99 stabilized at ~0.95s after full pool scale + restarts. keeping throttles in place for 45m then gradual rollback if stable.

maria (oncall): thanks everyone. handing off closed for oncall. :thumbsup:
